Theme

post a letter verb

also send a letter, mail a letter, I mailed the letter, send off a letter

classical

M-O s.v. mail

epistulam mittere

Other words

  • epistulam cursuī pūblicō trādere

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. mail

  • litterās dare (ad aliquem) — send a letter (to someone); literally, give a letter to the bearer

    phrase: ad with the person written to; the dative is the carrier · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.21: inde hās litterās dedī (Lewis & Short s.v. inde); Traupman 103: I mailed the letter yesterday, litterās heri dedī

    Letters went by hand, so “to post a letter” was to give it to someone travelling: litterās dare ad aliquem, to send someone a letter; litterās dare alicui, to hand a letter to someone to carry (Lewis & Short s.v. ad). Hence the letter-writer’s dedī, I sent.

Examples

  • Litterās heri dedī.

    I posted the letter yesterday.Traupman 103

See also postbox, stamp, envelope, postcard.
